tools.name: search_meeting_content
tools.description:
Search public meetings once across metadata and stored transcript text.

    Returns one card per meeting and native pagination metadata, without a total.
    Small current-text previews can be absent and do not establish timestamps.
    Text relevance can lag updates or match across untimed boundaries.
    Source transcripts searches stored text, including meetings without timed proof.

query.description: Analyzed words; put the whole query in double quotes for an analyzed phrase.
query.title: Query

cursor.description: Native next_cursor or previous_cursor from the same query and filters.
cursor.title: Cursor

tools.name: search_meetings_semantic
tools.description:
Find AI summaries by meaning; use search_meeting_content for stored words.

    Results carry relevance_score and a summary preview. Narrow with government,
    category_tag, topic or dates; get_meeting retrieves the full summary.

query.description: What to search for in plain language, e.g. 'short-term rental regulations' or 'police budget overtime'.
query.title: Query

government_id.description: Optional account_id (from find_local_governments) to restrict the search to one government.
government_id.title: Government Id

government_ids.description: Optional list of account_ids to search across several governments at once (e.g. to compare cities). Overrides government_id.
government_ids.title: Government Ids

category_tag.description: Optional meeting-type filter — an opaque category_tag from discover_meeting_vocabulary (not a guessable slug).
category_tag.title: Category Tag

topic.description: Optional topic filter — a topic name from discover_meeting_vocabulary, e.g. 'Affordable Housing'. Restricts to meetings that discussed it.
topic.title: Topic

match_type.description: Semantic only; use search_meeting_content for keyword searches.
match_type.title: Match Type

min_score.description: Optional semantic relevance floor 0-1 (default 0.4). Raise to return only strong matches; lower to widen recall.
min_score.title: Min Score

tools.name: list_recent_meetings
tools.description:
Browse meetings newest-first, optionally filtered by government, type, topic, or date.

    Use this for "what are the most recent meetings" or to page through a
    government's history. For topical questions, prefer `search_meetings_semantic`.

government_id.description: account_id to list meetings for (from find_local_governments). Omit to list across all governments.
government_id.title: Government Id

category_tag.description: Optional meeting-type filter — an opaque category_tag from discover_meeting_vocabulary (not a guessable slug; don't invent it).
category_tag.title: Category Tag

topic.description: Optional topic filter — a topic name from discover_meeting_vocabulary, e.g. 'Affordable Housing'.
topic.title: Topic

tools.name: get_meeting
tools.description:
Get a single meeting's full AI summary and topics.

    Set `include_transcript=true` to also retrieve the complete transcript text
    for direct quotation. Returns an error object if the meeting is not found.

meeting_id.description: The meeting_id returned by a search/list tool.
meeting_id.title: Meeting Id

include_transcript.description: If true, also fetch the full meeting transcript (can be long). Default false.
include_transcript.title: Include Transcript

tools.name: search_meeting_transcript
tools.description:
Use unified stored-text search inside one currently public meeting.

    Returns an optional current-text preview, without resolving timing. A text match
    can lack a literal preview; use get_meeting(include_transcript=true) for full source
    retrieval. This does not run a separate local scan or fuzzy passage ranking.

meeting_id.description: Canonical meeting_id returned by a search/list tool.
meeting_id.title: Meeting Id

query.description: Analyzed words or a whole quoted phrase.
query.title: Query

tools.name: find_local_governments
tools.description:
Discover which governments OpenPublica tracks near a coordinate.

    Returns nearby governments with their `account_id`, which you can pass to the
    other tools to scope results to a specific city or board. Note OpenPublica
    only covers a limited set of US localities; an empty result means none are
    tracked near that point yet.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location of interest.
longitude.title: Longitude

latitude.description: Latitude of the location of interest.
latitude.title: Latitude

tools.name: find_governments_by_name
tools.description:
Resolve a place *name* to the governments OpenPublica tracks there.

    Use this when you know a city/state name but not its coordinates — it returns
    matching governments with their `account_id` (prefix matches first), which you
    then pass to the search/list tools. Prefer this over `find_local_governments`
    when starting from a name rather than a latitude/longitude.

query.description: A place name to search for, e.g. 'Sacramento', 'San Francisco, CA', or a state like 'Texas'.
query.title: Query

tools.name: find_governments_by_zip
tools.description:
Resolve a ZIP code to nearby tracked governments.

    Convenience wrapper: geocodes the ZIP, then finds the governments OpenPublica
    tracks nearest that point. Returns their `account_id`s plus the resolved
    location. An empty `governments` list means none are tracked near that ZIP yet.

tools.name: get_government_info
tools.description: Get a tracked government's profile: name, location, and meeting categories.

include_weekly_summary.description: If true, include the AI-generated weekly digest (markdown). Default false.
include_weekly_summary.title: Include Weekly Summary

tools.name: get_government_stats
tools.description:
Get meeting-activity stats for a government over a recent window.

    Returns total meeting count, a per-day activity map, and a breakdown of
    meeting categories — useful for "how active has X been lately?" questions.

government_id.description: account_id of the government, or 'all' for corpus-wide stats.
government_id.title: Government Id

tools.name: discover_meeting_vocabulary
tools.description:
Discover the valid category and topic filter values before filtering a search.

    Meeting `category_tag`s are opaque UUIDs and topics have no fixed list, so you
    cannot guess them. Call this first to get the real values, then pass a returned
    `category_tag` (from `categories[].tags`) or `topic` string into
    `search_meetings_semantic` / `list_recent_meetings`. Scope with a government
    and/or date range; calls without explicit dates default to a recent window
    (returned as `default_window_days`).

government_id.description: Optional account_id to scope the vocabulary to one government.
government_id.title: Government Id

government_ids.description: Optional list of account_ids to scope to several governments. Overrides government_id.
government_ids.title: Government Ids

topic_limit.description: Max topics to return, most common first (1-200).
topic_limit.title: Topic Limit

tools.name: list_government_documents
tools.description:
List a government's adopted plan and budget documents.

    Each entry carries `covers` — every general-plan element that document
    answers for. A city that publishes one bound general plan satisfies all
    eight with the same PDF, so do not conclude an element is unpublished
    because no entry is named after it.

    `status` says what the entry offers: `converted` is searchable and readable;
    `superseded` is a retired edition, still stored but not searchable; and
    **`failed` means we hold this document and could not read it — it is not
    evidence the city published nothing.** Cite `source_url` in that case; it is
    always the city's own copy.

    An `availability` block appears ONLY when something is wrong with a
    document, and `availability.reason` says what. No `availability` key means
    there is nothing to report.

include_superseded.description: Also include prior editions retired by a newer document.
include_superseded.title: Include Superseded

tools.name: get_document
tools.description:
One document's metadata. Use read_document_pages to read it.

    If an `availability` key is present, read it before quoting figures: its
    `problems` are transcription-lint findings, most often a footnote marker
    that may have been merged into the number it annotates. No such key means
    the document transcribed cleanly.

document_id.description: Document id from list_government_documents or search_documents.
document_id.title: Document Id

tools.name: read_document_pages
tools.description:
Read a page range of a document as markdown.

    Pages are transcribed from rendered pixels, so tables and scanned text come
    through as text. A page that could not be transcribed appears as a marked
    hole rather than being silently dropped — if you see one, say so instead of
    reading past it.

    Text is assembled from page windows, so `covered` may be slightly wider than
    what you asked for; cite the page numbers in `covered`, not `requested`.

document_id.description: Document id from list_government_documents or search_documents.
document_id.title: Document Id

first_page.description: First page to read (1-based, as the PDF renders).
first_page.title: First Page

last_page.description: Last page to read. Spans longer than 40 pages are clamped to 40 from first_page.
last_page.title: Last Page

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description:
Search adopted plan and budget documents, returning page-cited excerpts.

    Each hit's `text` is a short passage around the match, not the full page —
    call read_document_pages with the hit's `first_page` to read it in context.

    Every hit carries `first_page`/`last_page` and `source_url`. Quote those
    when citing: the page number is what makes the claim checkable against the
    city's own copy.

    This is word matching, not semantic search — try the terms a plan would
    actually use. Only currently-served documents are searchable, so an empty
    result is not evidence the government has no such policy; check
    list_government_documents for what is held and what could not be read.

    A hit with `document_complete: false` comes from a document with
    transcription findings. Verify it against `source_url` before quoting a
    number from it.

query.description: Words to find in plan and budget text, e.g. 'accessory dwelling unit parking'.
query.title: Query

government_id.description: Optional account_id to restrict the search to one government.
government_id.title: Government Id

tools.name: get_coverage_overview
tools.description:
Get estimated stored-record totals, not publication-filtered coverage.

    Counts do not establish completeness, searchability or freshness. DC is
    reported separately from states as `includes_dc`.
